### **Job Description and Duties**


Caltrans Environmental Scientists perform a broad range of work concerning environmental issues related to protecting California's resources as related to transportation projects. Incumbents do field analyses; prepare environmental documents and technical studies, environmental permitting packages and regulatory permits; ensure compliance with various environmental laws and regulations; and conduct environmental protection, planning, and mitigation activities. Incumbents apply scientific methods and principles to analyze and evaluate available data on the effects of transportation projects on all aspects of the environment; prepare and review CEQA/NEPA and other technical documents to determine the effects; and implement mitigation strategies to lessen the impact of those projects.  

  

Under the general supervision of the Environmental Branch Chief, the incumbent is an interdisciplinary team member who must establish and maintain a professional working relationship with internal project delivery partners, various regulatory agencies, local partners and interested parties involved with Caltrans' projects. The incumbent must be solution oriented and will need to investigate innovative solutions to meet deliverables. This work requires strong oral and written skills with the specific ability to prepare technical reports as well as written and verbal correspondence. This position may require site visits, sometimes to remote areas.

### **Job Description and Duties**


The Measurement Assessment and Research Section (MARS) operates the Mobile Source Emissions Testing Facility in Sacramento, equipped with a heavy\-duty chassis dynamometer, advanced laboratory analyzers, Portable Emissions Measurement Systems (PEMS), and the Portable Emissions Acquisition System (PEAQS) to produce high\-quality, legally defensible emissions data. MARS’s mission is to support the development of heavy\-duty on\-road and off\-road vehicle regulations, strengthen emissions inventories, inform enforcement actions, advance the Clean Truck Check program, and drive research initiatives. Through surveillance testing of in\-use on\-road and off\-road heavy\-duty vehicles and equipment, MARS provides critical insights into real\-world emissions performance and regulatory effectiveness. MARS also serves as a platform for evaluating and demonstrating new test approaches, advancing innovative methods for measuring in\-use emissions, and improving testing capabilities. Working collaboratively with CARB mobile source workgroups, MARS develops and executes test plans, conducts comprehensive emissions testing, and delivers robust data analyses to guide policy decisions and protect air quality. These efforts provide the scientific foundation to achieve reductions in criteria pollutants, greenhouse gases, and toxic air contaminants from the heavy\-duty sector.  

MARS is seeking an Air Pollution Specialist to perform complex technical work related to in\-use emissions characterization of heavy\-duty (HD) on\-road and off\-road vehicles and equipment. The incumbent will conduct laboratory emissions testing using a heavy\-duty chassis dynamometer, perform on\-road emissions measurements with portable emissions measurement systems (PEMS), and ensure compliance with established test procedures, data quality objectives, and safety protocols. Duties include developing and applying analytical methods for emissions data processing, validation, and interpretation; analyzing large datasets using computational tools; designing and executing test plans; operating advanced emissions measurement systems; coordinating test resources; and preparing technical reports in support of regulatory programs, research initiatives, and emissions assessments, while working independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team to support CARB’s mission to protect air quality.  

This position offers a balanced mix of laboratory, field, and office\-based work and supports CARB’s mission by advancing in\-use emissions measurement techniques and evaluating emerging heavy\-duty vehicle technologies. The incumbent's position and reporting office is located at: CARB's \- Depot Park Facility, 8311 Galena Ave., Sacramento, CA 95828\. May require Statewide travel up to 20% of the time for fieldwork, training or for meetings.
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

* HAZWOPER training completed and up to date
* Asbestos coursework up to date and Certified Site Surveillance Technician (CSST) certification preferred.
* Progress towards professional certification (PE/PG) preferred
* Good communication and writing skills required
* Valid driver's license with driving record in good standing required

jobs.title: Capture Manager - Remediation and Technical
jobs.description:
**Job Overview**



APTIM is seeking a hands\-on Federal Capture Manager to help win strategic environmental remediation and technical services work. This role is ideal for an ambitious, proven capture professional who is ready to assume ownership of high\-priority pursuits and gain increased visibility and influence within a growing federal business. The position may be filled at the Senior Manager or Director level based on experience and demonstrated capture success.





The successful candidate will own assigned pursuits from early identification and qualification through capture, proposal development, negotiation and award. This individual will shape opportunities before solicitation release, develop customer and competitive intelligence, build executable win strategies, lead cross\-functional pursuit teams and remain personally accountable for advancing opportunities across the finish line. This is a capture lead position, not a proposal manager role. The Capture Manager will establish the strategy and maintain ownership and continuity throughout proposal development, negotiations and award.





The position will focus on federal environmental remediation pursuits, including investigations and remedial actions driven by CERCLA and RCRA, solicited under MATOCs, SATOCs, HTRW A\-E, and stand\-alone contracts to address environmental contaminants of concern (e.g. PFAS, VOCs, metals, radiological, etc.) for Department of War and civilian\-agency customers. The successful candidate will work directly with RTS leadership and experienced operational and technical teams, with an opportunity to grow into broader business\-development leadership based on performance.





**Key Responsibilities and Accountabilities**


* Contribute to the RTS growth strategy and build a qualified pipeline of strategic federal environmental opportunities with focus on contracts valued at $15M or greater.
* Own assigned pursuits from early identification and qualification through capture, proposal development, negotiation and award.
* Shape opportunities before solicitation release by developing a thorough understanding of customer missions, priorities, funding, acquisition strategies, evaluation criteria and procurement timelines.
* Develop and execute comprehensive capture plans, customer engagement strategies, competitive assessments, teaming strategies, win themes, discriminators and price\-to\-win approaches.
* Translate APTIM's technical capabilities, operational strengths and past performance into differentiated, customer\-focused solutions.
* Assemble and lead cross\-functional pursuit teams comprising operational, technical, contracts, legal, pricing, estimating and proposal resources.
* Lead opportunity qualification and governance reviews, presenting clear recommendations regarding competitive position, probability of win, required investment, resource needs and bid strategy.
* Build and maintain productive relationships with federal customers, industry partners, small\-business teammates and internal account and operational leaders.
* Monitor federal market conditions, customer priorities, competitors, acquisition trends and emerging technologies and translate that intelligence into actionable pursuit strategies.
* Maintain accurate pipeline information, capture milestones, pursuit investments, forecasts and action plans in APTIM's customer relationship management system.
* Manage multiple pursuits with urgency and discipline, communicate progress clearly and escalate barriers and resource requirements early.
* Capture lessons learned from wins and losses and apply them to improve future qualification, capture and proposal efforts.
* Represent APTIM at customer meetings, industry events, conferences and partner engagements when those activities support account and capture objectives.


**Required Qualifications**


* Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience.
* At least 10 years of combined experience in federal contracting, project delivery, client engagement, business development or capture management, including at least five years directly supporting or leading federal captures or strategic pursuits.
* Experience in federal environmental investigation, remediation, engineering, construction and technical services.
* Familiarity with one or more relevant environmental programs or disciplines, including CERCLA and RCRA, and experience with a variety of environmental contaminants including PFAS, VOCs, metals, and radiological.
* Experience pursuing work for the Department of War, USACE, NAVFAC, AFCEC, EPA, DOE or other federal environmental customers.
* Demonstrated experience leading opportunities through multiple stages of the federal acquisition lifecycle, from early qualification and shaping through proposal submission, negotiation and award.
* Experience capturing IDIQ vehicles, MATOCs, SATOCs, competitive task orders, competitive stand\-alone contracts, or similarly complex federal procurements.
* Demonstrated use of a disciplined capture process encompassing opportunity qualification, capture planning, customer and competitive analysis, win\-strategy development, decision gates and color\-team reviews.
* Experience leading cross\-functional teams that include proposal, technical, pricing, estimating, contracts, legal and operational personnel.
* Ability to develop persuasive written and oral presentations, influence diverse stakeholders and brief senior decision\-makers.
* Sound business and financial judgment, including experience evaluating pursuit investments, pricing considerations, contract risk and potential return.
* Willingness to travel for customer, partner and pursuit activities.


**Strongly Preferred Qualifications**


* Formal Shipley capture training or APMP certification.
* Demonstrated capture wins involving federal opportunities of meaningful size and complexity.

jobs.title: Portfolio Delivery Leader - Environmental Remediation Sector
jobs.description:
**Company Description** **Work with Us. Change the World.**


At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**  

AECOM is looking to hire a Portfolio Delivery Leaders (PDL) to oversee projects and project teams within our Environmental Remediation Group. The role is set up to be remote, however we will need the candidate to reside within the United States of America.


The PDL will report directly to the Practice Operations Lead, will serve as Project Director, and will be responsible for overseeing a portfolio of projects in the Remediation Practice of the Environment Business Line. The PDL will work closely with the Project Managers responsible for these projects to grow their financial acumen, project management capabilities, and drive overall project performance. The PDL will support the Practice Operations Lead in meeting Business Line objectives in the areas of financial profitability, project delivery, risk management, commercial terms evaluation, and budgeting and forecasting.


The ideal candidate for this opportunity has a natural drive and ability to communicate effectively with all levels of stakeholders, both internally and externally. The ideal PDL must have the ability to present information in a confident and concise manner to stakeholders. This opportunity requires someone who enjoys building relationships, is a team player, operates and responds in a fast\-paced environment with less than complete information, is well\-organized to understand priorities, and is familiar with the challenges projects with a variety of scopes and contract types bring.

**Responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:**

* Accountability for the planning, safe execution, and delivery of a portfolio of Environment projects at As Sold or better financial KPIs.
* Evaluating day\-to\-day project delivery performance, pricing strategies, risk management, forecasting and budgeting, and performance reporting for a ranging portfolio of Environment clients and projects.
* Interpreting project performance figures to support risk evaluation and financial forecasting.
* Providing proactive and hands\-on support to project managers to support strong financial monitoring, prevent project issues, address risks, and make recommendations to improve project performance. This includes analyzing project costs, billings and schedules, driving cash flow, trouble\-shooting problems both common and unique, supporting mitigation measures, and being “root cause oriented” in the resolution of issues.
* Ensuring appropriate scheduling tools and processes are in use by the project team and are supported by the Project Controller (PC) and/or PDL.
* Providing support to Project Managers (PM) by:
* Fully understanding applicable contracts
* Leading comprehensive project reviews covering scope, schedule, budget, risk, quality, resourcing, and client\-focused agenda topics
* Engaging project team at all milestones
* Proactive management of change (cost, revenue budget, schedule, etc.)
* Supporting dispute resolution, where required
* Supporting timely and accurate Estimate\-at\-Completion (EAC) preparation and review
* Proactively engaging project stakeholders
* Identifying and implementing appropriate tools to track physical % complete and translate to Earned Value Management
* Developing strong deputy project managers.
* In partnership with Project Controls leadership, mentoring and directing the work of Project Controls staff to appropriately support both the common and unique needs of their assigned portfolio.
* Assisting in the development and review of proposal resource plans, schedules and pricing that aligns with business line objectives and individual bid strategies. Supporting the client service/business development staff on key pursuits (e.g., initial evaluation of terms and conditions, commercial risk, and competitive advantage).
* In coordination with the Department or Program Manager, providing guidance in assigning projects and pursuit efforts to project managers.
* In partnership with the Department or Program Manager, continually evaluating performance of project managers within the portfolio, and mentoring project management staff to ensure timely, effective, and efficient performance of responsibilities.
* Fostering career growth of project managers.
* Developing PM risk competencies, including a strong contractual understanding of risk and contingency management
* Supporting project managers and project team members with invoicing and cash collection strategy. Reviewing unbilled/accounts receivable portfolios and making recommendations for improved performance to drive appropriate Days Sales Outstanding (DSO).
* Driving consistent project management practices and procedures in alignment with AECOM PM requirements.
* Evaluating and driving AECOM delivery excellence practices including Healthy Start project reviews.

 **Qualifications** **Minimum Requirements:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Environmental Sciences or comparable technical or business professional degree AND 4 years of relevant experience or demons

### **Job Description and Duties**


The Measurement Assessment and Research Section (MARS) operates the Mobile Source Emissions Testing Facility in Sacramento, equipped with a heavy\-duty chassis dynamometer, advanced laboratory analyzers, Portable Emissions Measurement Systems (PEMS), and the Portable Emissions Acquisition System (PEAQS) to produce high\-quality, legally defensible emissions data. MARS’s mission is to support the development of heavy\-duty on\-road and off\-road vehicle regulations, strengthen emissions inventories, inform enforcement actions, advance the Clean Truck Check program, and drive research initiatives. Through surveillance testing of in\-use on\-road and off\-road heavy\-duty vehicles and equipment, MARS provides critical insights into real\-world emissions performance and regulatory effectiveness. MARS also serves as a platform for evaluating and demonstrating new test approaches, advancing innovative methods for measuring in\-use emissions, and improving testing capabilities. Working collaboratively with CARB mobile source workgroups, MARS develops and executes test plans, conducts comprehensive emissions testing, and delivers robust data analyses to guide policy decisions and protect air quality. These efforts provide the scientific foundation to achieve reductions in criteria pollutants, greenhouse gases, and toxic air contaminants from the heavy\-duty sector.  

MARS is seeking an Air Pollution Specialist to perform complex technical work related to in\-use emissions characterization of heavy\-duty (HD) on\-road and off\-road vehicles and equipment. The incumbent will conduct laboratory emissions testing using a heavy\-duty chassis dynamometer, perform on\-road emissions measurements with portable emissions measurement systems (PEMS), and ensure compliance with established test procedures, data quality objectives, and safety protocols. Duties include developing and applying analytical methods for emissions data processing, validation, and interpretation; analyzing large datasets using computational tools; designing and executing test plans; operating advanced emissions measurement systems; coordinating test resources; and preparing technical reports in support of regulatory programs, research initiatives, and emissions assessments, while working independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team to support CARB’s mission to protect air quality.  

This position offers a balanced mix of laboratory, field, and office\-based work and supports CARB’s mission by advancing in\-use emissions measurement techniques and evaluating emerging heavy\-duty vehicle technologies. The incumbent's position and reporting office is located at: CARB's \- Depot Park Facility, 8311 Galena Ave., Sacramento, CA 95828\. May require Statewide travel up to 20% of the time for fieldwork, training or for meetings.

**Job Overview**



APTIM is seeking a hands\-on Federal Capture Manager to help win strategic environmental remediation and technical services work. This role is ideal for an ambitious, proven capture professional who is ready to assume ownership of high\-priority pursuits and gain increased visibility and influence within a growing federal business. The position may be filled at the Senior Manager or Director level based on experience and demonstrated capture success.





The successful candidate will own assigned pursuits from early identification and qualification through capture, proposal development, negotiation and award. This individual will shape opportunities before solicitation release, develop customer and competitive intelligence, build executable win strategies, lead cross\-functional pursuit teams and remain personally accountable for advancing opportunities across the finish line. This is a capture lead position, not a proposal manager role. The Capture Manager will establish the strategy and maintain ownership and continuity throughout proposal development, negotiations and award.





The position will focus on federal environmental remediation pursuits, including investigations and remedial actions driven by CERCLA and RCRA, solicited under MATOCs, SATOCs, HTRW A\-E, and stand\-alone contracts to address environmental contaminants of concern (e.g. PFAS, VOCs, metals, radiological, etc.) for Department of War and civilian\-agency customers. The successful candidate will work directly with RTS leadership and experienced operational and technical teams, with an opportunity to grow into broader business\-development leadership based on performance.

* Contribute to the RTS growth strategy and build a qualified pipeline of strategic federal environmental opportunities with focus on contracts valued at $15M or greater.
* Own assigned pursuits from early identification and qualification through capture, proposal development, negotiation and award.
* Shape opportunities before solicitation release by developing a thorough understanding of customer missions, priorities, funding, acquisition strategies, evaluation criteria and procurement timelines.
* Develop and execute comprehensive capture plans, customer engagement strategies, competitive assessments, teaming strategies, win themes, discriminators and price\-to\-win approaches.

* Assemble and lead cross\-functional pursuit teams comprising operational, technical, contracts, legal, pricing, estimating and proposal resources.
* Lead opportunity qualification and governance reviews, presenting clear recommendations regarding competitive position, probability of win, required investment, resource needs and bid strategy.
* Build and maintain productive relationships with federal customers, industry partners, small\-business teammates and internal account and operational leaders.
* Monitor federal market conditions, customer priorities, competitors, acquisition trends and emerging technologies and translate that intelligence into actionable pursuit strategies.
* Maintain accurate pipeline information, capture milestones, pursuit investments, forecasts and action plans in APTIM's customer relationship management system.
* Manage multiple pursuits with urgency and discipline, communicate progress clearly and escalate barriers and resource requirements early.
* Capture lessons learned from wins and losses and apply them to improve future qualification, capture and proposal efforts.
* Represent APTIM at customer meetings, industry events, conferences and partner engagements when those activities support account and capture objectives.


**Required Qualifications**


* Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience.
* At least 10 years of combined experience in federal contracting, project delivery, client engagement, business development or capture management, including at least five years directly supporting or leading federal captures or strategic pursuits.
* Experience in federal environmental investigation, remediation, engineering, construction and technical services.
* Familiarity with one or more relevant environmental programs or disciplines, including CERCLA and RCRA, and experience with a variety of environmental contaminants including PFAS, VOCs, metals, and radiological.
* Experience pursuing work for the Department of War, USACE, NAVFAC, AFCEC, EPA, DOE or other federal environmental customers.
* Demonstrated experience leading opportunities through multiple stages of the federal acquisition lifecycle, from early qualification and shaping through proposal submission, negotiation and award.
* Experience capturing IDIQ vehicles, MATOCs, SATOCs, competitive task orders, competitive stand\-alone contracts, or similarly complex federal procurements.
* Demonstrated use of a disciplined capture process encompassing opportunity qualification, capture planning, customer and competitive analysis, win\-strategy development, decision gates and color\-team reviews.
* Experience leading cross\-functional teams that include proposal, technical, pricing, estimating, contracts, legal and operational personnel.
* Ability to develop persuasive written and oral presentations, influence diverse stakeholders and brief senior decision\-makers.

* Willingness to travel for customer, partner and pursuit activities.
